title: Renewable energy: Africa leads, Iceland leads both

voiceover.text: Which continent runs on the most renewable energy?
In twenty twenty-one, African countries averaged fifty-six percent renewable.
The top country? The Democratic Republic of the Congo. Ninety-six percent.
But a person there uses about a hundred and thirty kilowatt-hours of electricity a year.
Much of Congo's renewable energy is wood and charcoal.
So look at share and use together. One country leads both.
Iceland. Eighty-two percent renewable, and fifty-one thousand kilowatt-hours per person.
Norway is second. Finland, third. It doubled its share since nineteen ninety.
We found this by joining two open datasets on Querious, right in your browser.
Then download the result, or connect it to your own tools.
The data is open. The question is yours.
